strings.2010: This is where you assign your trucks to delivery routes starting from a specific tile (building).  The starting point for the truck route is the tile name listed at the top of the window.
strings.2011: Truck route information is given in the large box on the left marked, Route.  The three buttons on the right are Delete Route, Delete Leg, and Add Leg.
strings.2012: If you highlight a route in the Route box, then click on Delete Route, the entire route will be removed and your trucks will no longer make deliveries to that destination.  Delete Leg allows you to remove only the last
strings.2013: destination in the route.  Add Leg allows you to create a new destination at the end of the current route.  When you select Add Leg, your cursor will change to one that says: Go Here.
strings.2014: Click the Go Here cursor on the building or road tile you want to use as your trucking destination.  The name of the selected tile is added to the Route list.  Keep doing this until you have
strings.2015: selected the final destination for the truck route.  All trucks assigned to this starting location will follow this one established route.  There is no need to list routing legs twice for multiple trucks.
strings.2016: The trucks will follow a specific path that you establish, then keep using that path for round trip deliveries until you re-assign them elsewhere or remove that route.  If you want your trucks to move faster by following an
strings.2017: existing dirt or paved road, you must click the Go Here cursor on the last tile of each straight section where the road curves, otherwise they will start taking shortcuts over rougher terrain which will slow them down.
strings.2018: Note that the Go Here cursor can only create a path to buildings or to terrain tiles that have been bulldozed or paved, so you cant Add a Leg to a regular terrain tile.
strings.2019: Either before or after you establish a route using the above method, you should select the Trucks button at the bottom of the routing window to assign trucks to that route.  Remember, all trucks assigned to the
strings.2020: starting location will follow the established route from that location.
strings.2021: If youre satisfied with your route and truck selections, click on the OK button.
strings.2022: This is where you make use of your inactive or stored trucks starting from a specific tile (building). The starting point for the truck route is the tile name listed at the top of the window.  The number of inactive
strings.2023: trucks in the warehouse is shown as the number Available.  The number of active trucks currently assigned to delivery routes are shown as the number Assigned. Click on the up and down arrows beside the Assigned
strings.2024: category to put more trucks in action, then click on the OK button.
strings.2025: This is where you choose an asset stored at this location and move it somewhere else in the same colony.  The tile location where the goods are stored is shown at the top of the window.  Choose an asset to transfer on the
strings.2026: left by using the up and down arrows and highlighting the name of the item. The number of those items available to be moved are shown on the right in the Quantities section.  Choose the number of items you wish to Move,
strings.2027: using the up and down arrows on the right, then click on OK.  If you change your mind, select Cancel.

strings.2031: This is where you keep track of the robots controlled by a specific Robot Command facility (each of which can control 10 robots).  Other information contained in this report shows you how the Robot Command itself is
strings.2032: doing. The top of the report tells you the name of the Robot Command facility.  You are also shown the Functional Status of the building, whether Operational or Idle; the condition of the staff required to operate
strings.2033: the Robot Command; the number of robots currently available and controlled by that facility; and the number of robots controlled by that facility which are actively assigned to tasks. For more specific information
strings.2034: on what the robots are doing and where they are, click on the Details button.
strings.2035: This is where you get information on what the robots are doing and where they are.  The Robot Command facility that controls this particular set of robots (up to ten) is shown at the top of the report.  You are also
strings.2036: shown the details on each robot: the type of robot, the remaining amount of life in its fuel cell, and where that robot is currently active (unless its idle and waiting to be assigned to a task).
strings.2037: Appropriate research must be completed before the monorail system becomes available, at which time the monorail tiles will show up in the tile picker (selection) window at the top center of the main game screen.
strings.2038: There are five basic components to a monorail system: the Monorail Station, the Monorail Power Transformer, the Monorail (track), the Monorail (track) Intersection, and the standard Tube connecting the Power Transformer
strings.2040: The Monorail Power Transformer can only be built at the end of a Tube connection.  The colony supplies life support, power, and the workers to operate each monorail section.
strings.2041: Monorail (track) tiles connect to Monorail Stations.  Monorail Stations can only be placed next to a Monorail Power Transformer or a Monorail (track) tile.  No Tube is required to connect a Power Transformer or
strings.2042: Monorail (track) to a Monorail Station.  The only Tube required for a monorail system is the one that connects the Power Transformer to the colony.
strings.2043: A Monorail (track) or a Monorail (track) Intersection can only be placed next to a Monorail Station or another Monorail (track).
strings.2044: When a complete monorail system has been established between two stations, and the power/resource connections have been made, the monorail line will become active.  If you have the CD version with the animated sequences
strings.2045: turned on, the monorail animation will run to announce the event.
strings.2046: Note that if two separate monorail lines become connected, a single train, instead of two, will make the complete circuit.
strings.2047: The Macromanagement interface allows you to do two things: sneak buildings into the rebel colony if you have an active trade agreement with them, and assign artificially intelligent computer managers to the administration
strings.2049: Assigning an AI to research in a laboratory is done through the research menu. This menu can be reached by clicking on a laboratory building, or through the Master Reports button in the main AI interface (reached by
strings.2050: clicking on the chrome ball icon in the lower left corner of the main game screen).
strings.2051: If you have an active trade agreement with the rebel colony, and a Trade Mission has been built for you there, you can sneak more buildings into the rebel colony.  This is not necessary for your survival, but it can be
strings.2052: used to your advantage.  If you want to prepare the rebel colony for the day when you take over its operation, you will have several buildings of your own choosing already built there.  If you want to undermine their
strings.2053: economy by building structures that will sap their resources, you have that capability.  You will not be allowed to build a factory or other obvious structures because shipping and storage operations would immediately
strings.2054: trigger too much attention from the authorities in the rebel colony.
strings.2055: The drawback to building in the rebel colony is that they will eventually notice what youre doing if you build several structures there.  When they do, they will probably break the trade agreement, preventing you from
strings.2056: trading with them or building further structures in their colony.  They will also take over ownership of any new buildings you created in their colony.
strings.2057: The Build in Rebel Colony button shows you a text list of buildings you can sneak into the rebel colony.  Highlight a building type by clicking on it, then select the OK button to confirm your decision.  The building will
strings.2058: be constructed in the normal amount of time, but it will use the resources of the rebel colony for construction and maintenance.
strings.2059: If you have completed the research leading to AI Managers, you will then have the option of assigning a few of your new artificial intelligence personalities to the management of your secondary colonies.  These new AI
strings.2060: managers are not as powerful as your primary AI assistant, so they are assigned to a specific colony and instructed to build structures that will allow that colony to specialize.  For example, you may want the AI manager
strings.2061: to build an agricultural colony that will stockpile food, which you can then truck or monorail to your main colony unless you want to use it for trade.
strings.2062: You will still need to check on the progress of your AI managers; they are primarily concerned about the colony systems and the orders you have given them, so the humans living in the colony get less attention.  You are
strings.2063: still responsible for the colony infrastructure and keeping the colonists alive.
strings.2064: When they first appear, you may find that your AI managers are not exactly following the instructions you have given them.  In some cases, you may find that an AI instructed to build an agricultural colony is building a
strings.2065: sea of communications towers instead.  If you see this situation, or if you want to slow down the use of resources by that colony, click on the De-Assign AI button.  Odd structures are built by unstable AI managers.
strings.2066: Appropriate research into AI personality problems will stabilize your managers.
